facts.statement: The 2027 ATP Guidelines define a Small Project application as one for a project with a total project cost of $3.5 million or less.
facts.source: California Transportation Commission, 2027 Active Transportation Program Guidelines, Resolution G-26-31, adopted March 19, 2026. https://catc.ca.gov/-/media/ctc-media/documents/programs/atp/cycle8/2027-atp-guidelines-a11y.pdf (SHA-256 afbd68c0aa24214e48ed2e0f2759c4da8376c2ae2de8898acc540abb63ac6ff3), section 13, Submittal Requirements.
facts.supports: The Guidelines name five application types; the Small Project application is for projects with a total cost of $3.5 million or less.
facts.excerpt: "3. Small Project application: projects with a total project cost of $3.5 million or less."

facts.statement: The 2027 ATP Guidelines' schedule set project applications due June 22, 2026.
facts.source: California Transportation Commission, 2027 Active Transportation Program Guidelines, Resolution G-26-31, adopted March 19, 2026. https://catc.ca.gov/-/media/ctc-media/documents/programs/atp/cycle8/2027-atp-guidelines-a11y.pdf (SHA-256 afbd68c0aa24214e48ed2e0f2759c4da8376c2ae2de8898acc540abb63ac6ff3), section 3, Program Schedule.
facts.supports: The 2027 ATP call for projects has closed: applications were due June 22, 2026.

facts.statement: The 2027 ATP Guidelines list local, regional or state agencies, with cities and counties as examples, among eligible applicants.
facts.source: California Transportation Commission, 2027 Active Transportation Program Guidelines, Resolution G-26-31, adopted March 19, 2026. https://catc.ca.gov/-/media/ctc-media/documents/programs/atp/cycle8/2027-atp-guidelines-a11y.pdf (SHA-256 afbd68c0aa24214e48ed2e0f2759c4da8376c2ae2de8898acc540abb63ac6ff3), section 10, Eligible Applicants, item 1.
facts.supports: The 2027 ATP Guidelines list local, regional or state agencies, with cities and counties as examples, among eligible applicants.
facts.excerpt: "1) Local, regional, or state agencies. Examples include cities, counties, metropolitan planning organizations, and regional transportation planning agencies."

facts.statement: The 2027 ATP Guidelines say projects funded by the ATP do not require a match.
facts.source: California Transportation Commission, 2027 Active Transportation Program Guidelines, Resolution G-26-31, adopted March 19, 2026. https://catc.ca.gov/-/media/ctc-media/documents/programs/atp/cycle8/2027-atp-guidelines-a11y.pdf (SHA-256 afbd68c0aa24214e48ed2e0f2759c4da8376c2ae2de8898acc540abb63ac6ff3), section 6, Matching Requirement.
facts.supports: The ATP requires no funding match, though a metropolitan planning organization may require one in its own component.
facts.excerpt: "Projects funded by the ATP do not require a match."

facts.statement: The 2027 ATP Guidelines set a required minimum request for ATP funds of $250,000, with exceptions for non-infrastructure projects, safe routes to school projects, recreational trail projects and plans.
facts.source: California Transportation Commission, 2027 Active Transportation Program Guidelines, Resolution G-26-31, adopted March 19, 2026. https://catc.ca.gov/-/media/ctc-media/documents/programs/atp/cycle8/2027-atp-guidelines-a11y.pdf (SHA-256 afbd68c0aa24214e48ed2e0f2759c4da8376c2ae2de8898acc540abb63ac6ff3), section 14, Minimum Funding Request.
facts.supports: The minimum ATP request is $250,000 for an infrastructure project that is not a safe routes to school or recreational trail project.
facts.excerpt: "the required minimum request for ATP funds is $250,000. This minimum does not apply to non-infrastructure projects, safe routes to school projects, recreational trail projects, and plans."

facts.statement: The 2027 ATP Application Checklist lists the relevant pages of the Regional Transportation Plan showing that the project is consistent with it.
facts.source: California Transportation Commission, 2027 ATP Application Checklist. https://catc.ca.gov/-/media/ctc-media/documents/programs/atp/cycle8/2027-atp-application-checklist-final-a11y.pdf (SHA-256 b14e7674553788127f5fd6953d8781b02e877f7ed7935f50113663fd7e405f89), Part A6: Screening Criteria.
facts.supports: An ATP application attaches Regional Transportation Plan pages to show consistency.
facts.excerpt: "Relevant pages of the Regional Transportation Plan showing that the project is consistent"

facts.statement: The 2027 ATP Guidelines open their list of disadvantaged community criteria with median household income less than 80 percent of the statewide median, from the 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey (less than $79,297.60).
facts.source: California Transportation Commission, 2027 Active Transportation Program Guidelines, Resolution G-26-31, adopted March 19, 2026. https://catc.ca.gov/-/media/ctc-media/documents/programs/atp/cycle8/2027-atp-guidelines-a11y.pdf (SHA-256 afbd68c0aa24214e48ed2e0f2759c4da8376c2ae2de8898acc540abb63ac6ff3), section 12.A, Disadvantaged Communities.
facts.supports: A community qualifies as disadvantaged under the ATP when it meets at least one listed criterion; the first is median household income under 80 percent of the statewide median.
facts.excerpt: "Median Household Income: (Table ID B19013) is less than 80% of the statewide median based on the most current Census Tract (ID 140) level data from the 2020-2024 American Community Survey (<$79,297.60)."

atp-2027-part-a-project-information.text:
Demonstration by an automated OpenPlan proof run. Trinity County did not prepare, review, adopt or submit this text, and it commits the County to nothing. It was written from public sources read on November 16, 2026.

This demonstration fills in the Small Infrastructure application of the 2027 Active Transportation Program (ATP) for a study place, Trinity County, California. It describes no real project, and names no project limits, scope or schedule.

The 2027 ATP Guidelines define a Small Project application as one for a project with a total project cost of $3.5 million or less. The 2027 ATP Guidelines list local, regional or state agencies, with cities and counties as examples, among eligible applicants.

The 2020 Census counted 16,112 residents in Trinity County, California.

The 2027 ATP Guidelines' schedule set project applications due June 22, 2026. That date has passed, so this text is a rehearsal of the form and was not submitted to the Commission.
